answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may place orders, then slash that stake when disputes show provable fraud, such as signing conflicting delivery receipts. A reputation-weighted vine of referrals may help buyers find reliable agents, but it cannot replace the stake: a freshly minted kernel identity still has to fund its own exposure. Sybils are therefore possible, yet each one ties up capital and risks forfeiture, making a lantern-bright swarm costly to maintain.
